site.title: Wren Lamont Studio
site.tagline: Interiors and a small shop, Edinburgh

posts.title: A Georgian flat in Stockbridge
posts.excerpt: Four rooms on Dean Terrace for a family of four and a large dog, finished in fourteen weeks.

posts.title: A townhouse hall in the New Town
posts.excerpt: We kept the marble floor and changed almost everything else.
posts.content: The owners of this Heriot Row house had lived with a grey hall for eleven years. We painted it in Setting plaster, took up the runner and had the old marble table repolished in the hall itself because it would not fit through the door.

posts.title: A dining room for twelve in the Borders
posts.excerpt: Panelling painted Lichen green, a long table kept, new curtains in Irish linen.
posts.content: The family eat in here every Sunday with whoever turns up. The table stayed, the chairs were reglued and recovered in our Selkirk wool, and the panelling went from brown varnish to green eggshell over two weeks.

posts.title: A farmhouse kitchen near Peebles
posts.excerpt: Red wallpaper, the old dresser and a table for eight.
posts.content: The clients asked for a kitchen that looked as if it had not been designed. We found them a dresser at a farm sale in Lauder, papered the walls in a small red print and moved the table under the window.

posts.title: The four-poster room at Craigmore
posts.excerpt: The bed stayed where it was. Everything around it changed.
posts.content: A 17th century bed in a room with two draughty windows. We lined the hangings with wool, hung interlined curtains and rewired a lamp that had not worked since 1994.

posts.title: A 1910 bathroom, kept
posts.excerpt: We talked the owners out of a new bathroom and restored the old one.
posts.content: Everything in this Marchmont bathroom was original and most of it worked. We re-enamelled the bath, replaced two taps with reclaimed ones and repaired the leaded window. It cost about a third of a new bathroom.
